## Code to run experiments on synthetic data

```{r import}
source(here("code", "bg_implement.R"), local = TRUE)
source(here("code", "bg_post.R"), local = TRUE)
```

Run ebpmf-bg full loop on simulated data.

```{r main-loop-controls}
a_grid <- c(0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000)
pi_mat <- cbind(
  mostly_background = c(0, 0, 0, 0.05, 0.95),
  broad_signal = c(0, 0.05, 0, 0, 0.95),
  near_zero_signal = c(0.05, 0, 0, 0, 0.95)
)
# Create data
settings <- list(
  n = 300, 
  p = 500, 
  K = 3,
  a = a_grid, # length-M Gamma shape list
  pi = pi_mat,
  seed = 1L,
  loading_mode = "single" # "single", "primary_secondary"
)

synthetic <- do.call(simulate_background_model, settings)

# Experiment switches.
init <- "deviance_kmeans" # "gamma", "deviance_kmeans", or "fasttopics"
oracle_f0 <- FALSE
oracle_pi <- FALSE
oracle_l <- FALSE

# Fit controls.
max_niter <- 400L
elbo_every <- 10L
fit_elbo_tolerance <- 1e-6
fit_elbo_patience <- 3L
```

```{r init}
initialization <- initialize_experiment_state(
  synthetic = synthetic,
  settings = settings,
  init = init,
  oracle_f0 = oracle_f0,
  oracle_pi = oracle_pi,
  oracle_l = oracle_l
)
state <- initialization$state
initialization_method <- initialization$method

# initialization$state retains the starting values for the diagnostic plots.
```

```{r main-loop}
# Main fitting
main_fit <- run_ebpmf_bg_cavi(
  state,
  synthetic$X,
  settings$a,
  max_niter = max_niter,
  elbo_every = elbo_every,
  fit_elbo_tolerance = fit_elbo_tolerance,
  fit_elbo_patience = fit_elbo_patience,
  estimate_pi = !oracle_pi,
  estimate_f0 = !oracle_f0
)

state <- main_fit$state
elbo_trace <- main_fit$elbo_trace
pi_trace <- main_fit$pi_trace
niter <- main_fit$completed_niter

# Summarize ELBO changes between stored checkpoints.
elbo_comparison <- data.frame(
  iteration = elbo_trace$iteration[-1L],
  elbo = tail(elbo_trace$elbo, -1L),
  change = diff(elbo_trace$elbo),
  relative_change = elbo_trace$relative_change[-1L]
)

fit_summary <- data.frame(
  maximum_iterations = max_niter,
  completed_iterations = niter,
  elbo_every = elbo_every,
  converged = main_fit$converged,
  oracle_f0 = oracle_f0,
  oracle_pi = oracle_pi,
  oracle_l = oracle_l,
  initialization = initialization_method
)

tail(elbo_comparison, 10L)
fit_summary

```

## Diagnostic Plots
The plots below provide diagnostic tools for interpreting EBPMF-BG runs. For the functions called in this section, see `bg_post.R`.

### Initial parameter values

The panels below show the state that enters the main CAVI loop. The initial feature matrix is
the variational mean `qF$mean`. Factor columns are shown in their actual fitting
order, without post-hoc alignment to the simulated truth.

```{r initial-parameters, fig.width=13, fig.height=9, dpi=150}
plot_initial_parameters(initialization$state, settings$a)
```

### Plot ELBO Convergence
Plot the log10 gap from the best recorded ELBO, omitting the final checkpoint.

```{r elbo-gap, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, dpi=150}
plot_elbo_gap(elbo_trace)
```

```{r}

```

### Aligned factor recovery for easier analysis

Factor labels and scales are not intrinsically identifiable: components may be
permuted. The comparisons below therefore align
components by their rate contributions (with cosine similarity) and adopt a common scale before
assessing recovery.

```{r align-normalize}
## Match fitted components to the generating components without rescaling them.
L_true <- synthetic$L
F_true <- synthetic$F
f0_true <- synthetic$f0
pi_true <- synthetic$pi
B_true <- sweep(F_true, 1L, f0_true, "*")
K <- ncol(L_true)

aligned <- align_k(synthetic, state)
L_hat <- aligned$L
F_hat <- aligned$F
B_hat <- aligned$B
pi_hat <- aligned$pi
f0_hat <- state$f0
best_permutation <- aligned$permutation

## L[, k] * B[, k]' is unchanged if L[, k] is divided by c and
## B[, k] is multiplied by c. Use mean(L[, k]) = 1 as a convention.

true_canonical <- canonicalize(L_true, B_true)
hat_canonical  <- canonicalize(L_hat, B_hat)

L_true_plot <- true_canonical$L
L_hat_plot  <- hat_canonical$L

B_true_plot <- true_canonical$B
B_hat_plot  <- hat_canonical$B

plot_factor_recovery(true_canonical, hat_canonical)
```

### Plot mixture proportions convergence

```{r mixprop-iter, fig.width=15, fig.height=5}
plot_mixprop_convergence(pi_trace, pi_true, pi_hat, best_permutation, settings$a)
```

Solid lines show the estimated mixture proportions recorded during the main CAVI run, while matching dashed lines show the generating proportions.

### Plot reconstructed Poisson rate

```{r rate-lineplot}
plot_lambda(L_true, B_true, L_hat, B_hat)
```

The reconstructed-rate plot compares
\(\lambda=L(f_0F)^\mathsf{T}\), the quantity that directly determines the
Poisson likelihood. Note strong rate recovery is possible even when the individual factors
are not recovered exactly.

### Background recovery

```{r bg-lineplot, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
plot_bgquality(L_true, L_hat, f0_true, f0_hat)
```

The plots compare the raw true and estimated `f0` values.

### Plot true vs. estimated loadings, factors

```{r lf-heatmap, fig.width=16, fig.height=18, out.width="100%", dpi=150}
plot_lf(true_canonical, hat_canonical)
```

### Plot true vs. estimated mixture proportions

```{r mixprop-heatmap, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5, out.width="100%", dpi=150}
plot_mixprop(pi_true, pi_hat, settings$a)
```

The annotated cells report \(\pi_{mk}\) directly. Columns of the estimated
matrix use the same factor matching as the preceding plots, while rows
correspond to the Gamma components identified by their shape parameters
`settings$a`.

### Plot if f0 error is correlated with f_jk error

```{r error-compensate, eval=!oracle_f0}
plot_compensate(B_true_plot, B_hat_plot, f0_true, f0_hat)
```

If correlation high, error in f0 is offsetting error in F. On the other hand, if the plot is concentrated near the red vertical line at zero, it means little compensation.
